title: Bounded sensor errors kept four joint-exposure contrasts positive in North Wales domes in August-September 2021
abstract: We tested how bounded sensor errors can change heated-minus-ambient joint-exposure contrasts in a public wildflower experiment. We used 1,464 complete hourly records in August and September 2021. Joint exposure meant air vapor pressure deficit of at least 2 kPa and ozone of at least 60 ppb. At the 80 and 110 ppb peak targets, all four monthly contrasts had positive sharp lower limits under errors of up to 0.5 C, 5 relative-humidity percentage points and 5 ppb ozone. Lower limits ranged from 0.83 to 5.83 percentage points. Twice these error bounds permitted zero in all four comparisons. The 30 ppb target had zero main-cutoff joint hours. We prove the bounds by monotonic event indicators and give tipping error scales. The error limits are assumptions, not measured sensor performance. The method permits errors to vary across hours and sensors. One site, one year, one dome per treatment and a shared ambient weather reference limit inference. No plant injury, species change or causal warming effect was tested. This extends prior analyses of the same records and is not independent replication. Code, aggregate bounds, source hashes and an independent numerical check are included.

display.caption: Sharp joint-exposure share bounds under errors up to 0.5 C, 5 humidity percentage points and 5 ppb ozone. Dots show the released-record contrasts. Bounds are deterministic and conditional, not confidence intervals.
